name: Degrees of games
oneLine: Games come in three degrees of intensity: first (shareable with your social circle), second (kept private), and third (ends in real damage).
whatYouDid: You classified Omar's bar-room grumbling as first-degree Kick Me - casual, public, time-structuring - rather than second or third degree.

fromBook.quote: ...is one which is played for keeps, and which ends in the surgery, the courtroom or the morgue.

expand.definition: A first-degree game has an outcome the player is happy to talk about socially - first-degree games make up a large share of time-structuring at parties. A second-degree game has an outcome the player would rather not make public. A third-degree game, in Berne's words, is "played for keeps" and ends in real damage.
expand.otherFraming: The same named game - Kick Me, Rapo, NIGYSOB - can be played at any of the three degrees; the degree isn't fixed by which game it is, it's set by how far the player is willing to take it.
expand.tryThisToday: Next time you catch yourself mid-game, ask which degree you're currently willing to play it at - naming the ceiling out loud is often enough to keep it there.
